newArtifact.name: AuditEvent
newArtifact.identityNotesMd: The R6 counterpart is present with stable canonical identity. Status changed from draft to active, which is notable but not a breaking identity change.

narrativeReportMd:
# AuditEvent R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
AuditEvent keeps the same canonical identity but has substantial local breaking changes. R6 redesigns timing, outcome, agent identity, coded classifiers, source/site, authorization, and entity details.

## Scope
Only AuditEvent-owned StructureDefinition changes are findings. Inherited Resource, DomainResource, Element, Extension, BackboneElement, and datatype changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Most work is structural: primitive or Coding fields become backbone, choice, Reference, or CodeableConcept fields. Agent identity is tightened, old agent/entity fields are removed, and new R6 context fields create downgrade gaps.

## Highest-impact findings
The most significant changes are outcome reshaping, mandatory agent.who, Coding-to-CodeableConcept classifier conversion, entity field removals, and entity.detail type changes.

## Findings requiring human review
Review outcome code mapping, authorization semantics, media/entity lifecycle preservation, terminology conformance, and R6-to-R4 downgrade policy.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes could have been staged through aliases, choices, deprecated fields, or profiles. R6 generally chose a cleaner/richer model, so cross-version transforms are mandatory.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: AuditEvent has high-impact local breaking changes: outcome restructuring, mandatory agent identity, Coding-to-CodeableConcept classifiers, entity removals, entity.detail typing, and several R6 downgrade gaps. The main uncertainty is official mapping intent for outcome codes and removed fields.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Use an AuditEvent-specific transform: rename and reshape time/outcome fields, populate agent.who, wrap Coding as CodeableConcept, preserve removed agent/entity data through policy, and define R6-to-R4 downgrade extensions for new R6 fields.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both core StructureDefinitions are present and the R6 counterpart is unambiguous. Confidence is medium for terminology/semantic mapping because official expansions, ConceptMaps, and narrative change notes were unavailable.

findings.title: AuditEvent.period was replaced by occurred[x]

oldState.summary: R4 used optional `AuditEvent.period` of type Period.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used optional `AuditEvent.period` of type Period.

newState.summary: R6 uses optional `AuditEvent.occurred[x]` with Period or dateTime.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses optional `AuditEvent.occurred[x]` with Period or dateTime.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same time-of-event semantics, broadened into a choice.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `period` is not a valid R6 element. R6 `occurredPeriod` can map back by renaming, but `occurredDateTime` is not exactly R4-representable without synthesizing a Period or using an extension.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 `period` for Period values and add a separate optional instant/dateTime field, with guidance or an invariant against using both.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable: express either a point time or a period under a clearer event-occurrence name. A less-breaking design could preserve R4 `period`, but it would not provide a single clean `occurred[x]` choice and would need rules to prevent conflicting time fields. Because that duplicate-representation risk is material, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would retain `AuditEvent.period` unchanged for existing Period content and add an optional new dateTime-bearing element for instantaneous events. That would preserve R4 instances, but implementers would have to reconcile `period` versus the new instant field, and the deprecated R4 representation could remain indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old Period instances but creates two event-time representations and leaves the less clear R4 name in the base model.

findings.narrativeMd: The activity time field was renamed and broadened. R4 instances with `period` need a field-name transform to validate in R6; R6 `occurredDateTime` needs downgrade policy.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `period` is not a valid R6 element. R6 `occurredPeriod` can map back by renaming, but `occurredDateTime` is not exactly R4-representable without synthesizing a Period or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `period` to `occurredPeriod`. For R6-to-R4, define whether dateTime becomes a zero-duration Period or an extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 Period-valued event timing moves from `period` to the R6 choice `occurred[x]`. Existing instances and generated properties need a rename transform, and R6 dateTime occurrences need a downgrade convention. The R6 design is still proportionate because a single occurrence choice aligns the instant-or-interval semantics better than keeping parallel time fields.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.period]: 0..1 Period.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.occurred[x]]: 0..1 choice of Period or dateTime.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 AuditEvent is FMM 3/trial-use, so compatibility matters for event timing, but the content is not normative/FMM 5; the clearer occurrence choice can justify a focused transform.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `period` property is not an R6 AuditEvent element; R6 `occurredDateTime` also creates limited R6-to-R4 loss unless converted to a Period or extension.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have retained `period` for intervals and added a separate instant/dateTime field. That would preserve R4 instances but leaves two same-purpose timing representations and requires conflict rules, so the alternative has material modeling cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a real hard break with only a partial less-breaking alternative; I view the alternative tradeoff as large enough that the break is probably OK.

findings.title: AuditEvent.outcome changed from primitive code to BackboneElement

oldState.summary: R4 `outcome` was a primitive code with required binding and `outcomeDesc` was a sibling string.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `outcome` was a primitive code with required binding and `outcomeDesc` was a sibling string.

newState.summary: R6 `outcome` is a BackboneElement with mandatory `outcome.code` Coding and repeating `outcome.detail` CodeableConcept.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `outcome` is a BackboneElement with mandatory `outcome.code` Coding and repeating `outcome.detail` CodeableConcept.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `"outcome":"0"` is invalid in R6. R6 details and multiple/alternate outcome codings cannot be represented losslessly in R4, which had one code plus one text description.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain primitive `outcome` and `outcomeDesc` while adding optional structured outcome coding/detail fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 adds a richer outcome model with a mandatory `outcome.code` Coding and repeatable details, which better supports alternate code systems and precise outcome information. Preserving the R4 primitive shape would be possible only by running parallel old and new outcome representations or by weakening the structured model. Given the high conflict and downgrade ambiguity around success/failure semantics, the breaking design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A staged design could keep `outcome` as the R4 code, keep `outcomeDesc`, and add new optional structured detail/coding elements. That would avoid invalidating R4 instances, but systems would need precedence rules when both the primitive and structured outcome are populated, and the legacy low-granularity representation might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve R4 wire format, but splits one outcome across legacy primitive and richer structured representations.

examples.examplesMd: Outcome code mapping needs terminology review.

findings.narrativeMd: `outcome` is a high-impact wire-format change. Generated models, enum switches, serializers, and reporting code that expect a primitive code must now handle a nested object and detail list.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `"outcome":"0"` is invalid in R6. R6 details and multiple/alternate outcome codings cannot be represented losslessly in R4, which had one code plus one text description.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map primitive outcome into `outcome.code`; map `outcomeDesc` to `outcome.detail.text`. Use an explicit ConceptMap or local policy for R4 codes 0/4/8/12.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Outcome is a central audit result field, and R6 changes both the wire shape and the terminology model: a primitive R4 code plus optional description becomes a backbone with mandatory Coding and repeatable detail. Migration is not just syntactic because R4 codes 0/4/8/12 come from the audit-event-outcome code system while R6 points the outcome value set at issue-severity. That makes lossless, consistently reviewed mapping important.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.outcome]: 0..1 code with required audit-event-outcome binding; AuditEvent.outcomeDesc is 0..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.outcome]: BackboneElement with outcome.code 1..1 Coding and outcome.detail 0..* CodeableConcept.
Local terminology: R4 ValueSet-audit-event-outcome includes http://hl7.org/fhir/audit-event-outcome codes 0, 4, 8, 12; R6 ValueSet-audit-event-outcome includes http://hl7.org/fhir/issue-severity.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the burden for a high-value audit/security path even though it is not normative. The result of an audited event is common enough and accountable enough that the break needs strong rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `outcome` as a primitive code and `outcomeDesc` are rejected by the R6 shape; R6 structured detail and issue-severity coding are lossy or judgment-dependent when downgraded to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A staged base design could have kept the R4 primitive `outcome` and `outcomeDesc` as deprecated elements while adding structured outcome coding/detail under new names. That duplicates outcome representations and needs precedence rules, but for a central result field the tradeoff may be preferable to an immediate shape and code-system break.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing high impact and partial alternative assessment, but I weigh the terminology remap and central audit semantics more heavily, so this deserves Revisit rather than being treated as probably justified.

findings.title: AuditEvent.agent.who became mandatory while requestor became optional

newState.summary: R6 requires `agent.who` 1..1, makes `requestor` optional with meaningWhenMissing=false, and expands who target profiles.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires `agent.who` 1..1, makes `requestor` optional with meaningWhenMissing=false, and expands who target profiles.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 agents without `who` become R6-invalid. R6 agents without `requestor` or with new target types are not valid R4 without defaults, target reduction, or extensions.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `agent.who` optional in the base resource and require or warn on it through profiles, best-practice rules, or implementation guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of stronger accountability is reasonable: `agent.who` ties the audit event to a specific actor or identifier. A profile-only or warning-only alternative would preserve R4 instances without `who`, but it would not deliver the same base-level identity guarantee and could perpetuate anonymous audit records. That accountability tradeoff is material, so the break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking alternative is to leave `agent.who` at 0..1 and use profiles, conformance expectations, or best-practice invariants to require it where identity is known. This preserves R4 data but gives base R6 consumers less assurance that each agent is attributable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids invalidating anonymous R4 agents but fails to guarantee agent identity in base R6 AuditEvents.

findings.narrativeMd: Agent identity is now required. Historical R4 logs with anonymous or only network/requestor agents can fail R6 validation; R6 logs can omit requestor or reference target types outside R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 agents without `who` become R6-invalid. R6 agents without `requestor` or with new target types are not valid R4 without defaults, target reduction, or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Populate `agent.who` from reliable identifiers/display values. Do not invent identities silently. For downgrade, add `requestor:false` when absent and preserve unsupported targets with extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 requires every agent to carry `who`, while R4 allowed an agent identified only by requestor, name, alternate id, or network details. This can invalidate sparse historical audit records and affects generated validators. The R6 accountability goal is strong, though: an audit event whose active participant cannot be tied to a resource, identifier, or display is weak evidence.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.agent.who]: min 0, target profiles PractitionerRole, Practitioner, Organization, Device, Patient, RelatedPerson.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.agent.who]: min 1, expanded targets including CareTeam, DeviceDefinition, Group, HealthcareService.
R4 AuditEvent.agent.requestor min 1; R6 AuditEvent.agent.requestor min 0 with meaningWhenMissing false.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means existing audit log producers deserve compatibility consideration, but the security/accountability purpose of AuditEvent supports a higher base requirement for agent identity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 agent without `who` fails R6 validation; R6 agents without explicit `requestor` or using newly allowed target types require defaults, reduction, or extensions for R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have left `agent.who` optional and used profiles, best-practice warnings, or IG requirements to demand identity. That would preserve anonymous R4 agents, but it would not give base R6 consumers a computable identity guarantee, which is a material safety/security tradeoff.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies high impact and only a partial less-breaking alternative; the accountability rationale is strong enough that the break is probably OK.

findings.title: Several optional agent fields were removed or reworked

newState.summary: R6 removes altId/name/media, directs identifiers/display into `agent.who`, and replaces network with `agent.network[x]` Reference(Endpoint)|uri|string.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes altId/name/media, directs identifiers/display into `agent.who`, and replaces network with `agent.network[x]` Reference(Endpoint)|uri|string.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using removed agent fields are R6-invalid. R6 Endpoint references cannot be fully represented in R4 network.address/type.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `altId`, `name`, `media`, and/or the old network backbone while adding the new `who` and `network[x]` guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 cleanup toward `who.identifier`, `who.display`, and `network[x]` is coherent, but the local evidence does not show that removing every optional R4 field was necessary. Several old fields could have remained deprecated without blocking the R6 model, especially `media` and `network.type`, which do not have exact same-path replacements. Because the less-breaking alternative is incomplete and duplicative but still plausible, the break is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A staged base design could retain the old optional scalar fields as deprecated, add or prefer `who` and `network[x]`, and document precedence when both old and new fields are present. The cost is a larger agent model and possible divergence between `altId`/`name` and `who`, or between the old network backbone and `network[x]`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common legacy agent details, but creates overlapping identity and network representations with conflict-resolution burden.

examples.examplesMd: Media and network type require local policy.

findings.narrativeMd: The agent subtree moved from dedicated scalar fields toward Reference and choice-based modeling. Some old values are migratable, but media and network type can be lost.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using removed agent fields are R6-invalid. R6 Endpoint references cannot be fully represented in R4 network.address/type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move altId/name to `who.identifier`/`who.display`; map network addresses to networkString/networkUri; preserve media and network.type in extensions or entity modeling when needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Several optional agent details disappear or move into more general R6 representations. Alternate id and name can usually move into `who.identifier` and `who.display`, and a network address can move into `networkString` or `networkUri`; however media and the old network type do not have an equivalent same-path replacement. Because these are audit attribution details, silent loss would be material.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition contains AuditEvent.agent.altId, agent.name, agent.media, and agent.network.address/type.
R6 StructureDefinition contains mandatory AuditEvent.agent.who and AuditEvent.agent.network[x] Reference(Endpoint)|uri|string; the R4 altId/name/media/network backbone paths are absent.
R6 AuditEvent.entity.agent maps to DICOM ActiveParticipant.MediaType, indicating media semantics moved rather than remaining as a direct agent field.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not forbid redesign, but it raises concern when mature audit/security data fields are removed without exact replacements.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances populated with removed agent fields fail R6 validation; some values can be transformed, but media and network type require local preservation policy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept the old optional fields as deprecated while preferring `who` and `network[x]`. That creates overlapping identity/network representations, but the old fields are optional and the tradeoff seems modest compared with losing audit attribution details.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's medium impact and partial less-breaking alternative are directionally right; I classify the design as Revisit because deprecating optional legacy fields looks plausible.

findings.title: purposeOfEvent and agent.purposeOfUse were renamed and broadened to authorization

oldState.summary: R4 used `purposeOfEvent` and `agent.purposeOfUse`, CodeableConcept with extensible v3 PurposeOfUse binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `purposeOfEvent` and `agent.purposeOfUse`, CodeableConcept with extensible v3 PurposeOfUse binding.

newState.summary: R6 uses `authorization` and `agent.authorization`, CodeableConcept with example binding and broader security-context requirements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `authorization` and `agent.authorization`, CodeableConcept with example binding and broader security-context requirements.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Comments preserve global-vs-agent-specific guidance while broadening semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old purpose fields are invalid in R6. R6 authorization values outside PurposeOfUse are not cleanly R4-representable.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `purposeOfEvent` and `agent.purposeOfUse` with broadened definitions/bindings, or add `authorization` while accepting the old names during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of recording broader authorization/security context is reasonable, but the changed fields keep the same CodeableConcept shape and largely preserve the old global-versus-agent split. Because the goal could be met by broadening the existing fields' definitions and bindings, living with the less ideal R4 names would have avoided invalidating old instances. The rename therefore looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible R6 base design could keep `purposeOfEvent` and `agent.purposeOfUse`, update their definitions to cover authorization/security context beyond purpose-of-use, and weaken the bindings as R6 did. If a clearer `authorization` name was still desired, it could be added as a companion with explicit precedence rules, but ordinary migration guidance alone should not be counted as the alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains less precise R4 names, but avoids a same-type rename break with modest long-term cost.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a field-name break plus semantic broadening from purpose-of-use to authorization/security context. It can affect privacy and access-control interpretation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old purpose fields are invalid in R6. R6 authorization values outside PurposeOfUse are not cleanly R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move purpose values to authorization fields. Review non-purpose authorization/security tags during downgrade and preserve them with extensions if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 purpose-of-use fields are renamed to authorization fields while retaining the same CodeableConcept cardinality pattern and the same global-vs-agent split. R6 broadens the meaning and weakens the binding, but the old field names could have carried that broader definition during a transition. This is a direct wire-name break in privacy/security context data.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: AuditEvent.purposeOfEvent 0..* CodeableConcept and AuditEvent.agent.purposeOfUse 0..* CodeableConcept with extensible PurposeOfUse binding.

R6 StructureDefinition: AuditEvent.authorization 0..* CodeableConcept and AuditEvent.agent.authorization 0..* CodeableConcept with example PurposeOfUse binding and broader security-context requirements.
R6 authorization elements list aliases PurposeOfEvent and PurposeOfUse.
freshReview.fmmEffect: For FMM 3/trial-use security/audit content, a same-shape rename affecting purpose and authorization semantics needs a stronger justification than a low-maturity cleanup would.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `purposeOfEvent` and `agent.purposeOfUse` are not R6 element names; R6 authorization values outside purpose-of-use are not cleanly representable in R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A low-cost less-breaking design exists: keep the R4 names, broaden their definitions and bindings, and optionally add authorization aliases or companion elements later. The tradeoff is living with less precise names, but that is a small cost relative to invalidating same-type data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly flags a medium-impact break with an available less-breaking base design.

findings.title: Several coded classifier elements changed Coding shape or weakened bindings

oldState.summary: R4 used Coding for type, subtype, source.type, entity.role, and entity.securityLabel; agent.type was extensible-bound CodeableConcept.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used Coding for type, subtype, source.type, entity.role, and entity.securityLabel; agent.type was extensible-bound CodeableConcept.

newState.summary: R6 uses CodeableConcept for those classifiers and weakens several bindings to example or preferred.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses CodeableConcept for those classifiers and weakens several bindings to example or preferred.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old Coding JSON with `system`/`code` directly on the element is invalid in R6 CodeableConcept paths. R6 multiple codings/text are lossy when downgraded to R4 Coding fields.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 Coding elements and loosen bindings while adding companion CodeableConcept fields only where alternate codings/text are needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is substantial: classifier fields become CodeableConcepts and several bindings are relaxed so systems can carry multiple codings, text, and locally sliced terminology. Keeping the R4 Coding shape would preserve old instances but would only partly meet the goal unless parallel CodeableConcept fields were introduced. That duplicate classifier model would create selection and search ambiguity, so the breaking design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could leave `type`, `subtype`, `source.type`, `entity.role`, and `entity.securityLabel` as Coding while weakening bindings, then add companion CodeableConcept elements where needed. This would preserve R4 wire shape, but consumers would have to decide which classifier representation is authoritative when both are present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves direct R4 Coding JSON but duplicates classifier representations and weakens consistent querying.

findings.narrativeMd: Classifier paths are pervasive. Coding-to-CodeableConcept changes break JSON shape and generated classes, and binding weakening changes validation/conformance behavior for security/audit classifiers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old Coding JSON with `system`/`code` directly on the element is invalid in R6 CodeableConcept paths. R6 multiple codings/text are lossy when downgraded to R4 Coding fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old Coding values in CodeableConcept.coding. For downgrade, choose a primary coding deterministically and preserve additional codings/text. Re-profile R6 if stronger bindings remain required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 converts several classifier fields from single Coding values to CodeableConcepts and relaxes some bindings. R4 JSON with `system` and `code` directly under the element will not validate in R6, and R6 values with multiple codings or text need a primary-coding policy for downgrade. Still, the R6 model better supports alternate terminology, local codings, and descriptive text for classifier data.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: AuditEvent.type, subtype, source.type, entity.role, and entity.securityLabel are Coding-valued classifier paths.
R6 StructureDefinition: those classifier paths are CodeableConcept-valued, with several bindings changed to example or preferred.
R4 AuditEvent.agent.type is CodeableConcept with extensible binding; R6 keeps CodeableConcept but changes the binding to preferred.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the compatibility bar because these classifier paths are useful for filtering, access control, and audit analysis, but the maturity level still allows model cleanup when the alternative would duplicate classifications.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: direct R4 Coding JSON is invalid for R6 CodeableConcept paths; R6 multiple codings/text cause R6-to-R4 loss unless one coding is selected and the rest preserved elsewhere.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the Coding fields and added parallel CodeableConcept fields only where richer representation was needed. That would preserve R4 instances but creates duplicate classifier sources and ambiguous search/filter semantics, so the less-breaking option has substantial long-term cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high impact and partial alternative assessment matches the fresh review; the break is real but proportionate.

findings.title: AuditEvent.source.site changed from string to Reference(Location), and source.observer target widened

oldState.summary: R4 `source.site` was a string and source.observer did not target CareTeam.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `source.site` was a string and source.observer did not target CareTeam.

newState.summary: R6 `source.site` is Reference(Location), and source.observer can reference CareTeam.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `source.site` is Reference(Location), and source.observer can reference CareTeam.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 site strings fail R6 validation. R6 Location references and CareTeam observers cannot be represented in R4 without reduction or extension.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `source.site` as a string and add a separate optional Location reference for systems that can identify the site resource.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Replacing the site string with `Reference(Location)` improves resolvability, but the R4 string already captured a logical site label and could have remained valid. The source.observer target widening is not itself R4-to-R6 breaking. A companion Location reference would meet much of the R6 goal with less breakage, though it would require reconciliation rules when both string and reference are present, so the change is not clearly justified rather than plainly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would keep `AuditEvent.source.site` as the legacy string and add a new optional Location reference, or otherwise permit a textual site alongside a resolvable Location. This preserves R4 instances but carries a material risk that the text and Location reference disagree or that implementations keep using only the weaker string.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy site labels but introduces possible divergence between textual and referenced site values.

findings.narrativeMd: Source site changed from primitive text to a resource reference, affecting validators, serializers, and indexes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 site strings fail R6 validation. R6 Location references and CareTeam observers cannot be represented in R4 without reduction or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old strings to `source.site.display` or create Location references. Define downgrade handling for Location and CareTeam references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 source site was a simple logical site label; R6 requires a Location reference object. A display-only reference can carry the old text, but historical strings no longer validate as-is and resolvable Location identity cannot always be manufactured during migration. The source observer target widening is additive, but the site type replacement is a direct break.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.source.site]: 0..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.source.site]: 0..1 Reference(Location).
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.source.observer] adds CareTeam as a target profile.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means a source-identification path in a security/audit resource deserves preservation unless the replacement's benefit clearly requires breaking old values.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `source.site` string is not the R6 Reference shape; R6 Location references and CareTeam observers need reduction or extension when downgraded to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have kept the string site label and added a separate optional Location reference. That creates possible disagreement between text and reference, but it is a modest, localized tradeoff and would preserve common legacy site labels.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the medium impact, but I give more weight to the practical string-plus-reference base alternative, so the finding merits Revisit.

findings.title: AuditEvent.entity.type, entity.lifecycle, and entity.name were removed

oldState.summary: R4 entity had optional `type` Coding, `lifecycle` Coding, and `name` string.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 entity had optional `type` Coding, `lifecycle` Coding, and `name` string.

newState.summary: R6 removes those paths; `entity.what` guidance covers string names via display/identifier, but no direct lifecycle replacement exists.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes those paths; `entity.what` guidance covers string names via display/identifier, but no direct lifecycle replacement exists.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Removed entity fields fail R6 validation. R6 cannot reconstruct them unless preserved in detail, extensions, or related resources.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `entity.type`, `entity.lifecycle`, and `entity.name` as deprecated elements while preferring `what`, `role`, security labels, or detail conventions where appropriate.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local definitions show important R4 audit semantics, especially lifecycle, with no exact R6 replacement. Removing optional fields invalidates old instances and risks data loss, while retaining them as deprecated would not block the R6 guidance to use `entity.what.display` or more structured references. Because the compatibility-preserving design appears practical with moderate tradeoff, this break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep the three R4 elements, mark them deprecated or discouraged, and clarify preferred R6 mappings. `entity.name` could remain a legacy textual descriptor, while `entity.type` and `entity.lifecycle` could preserve legacy audit classifications until implementations adopt more structured conventions. The tradeoff is that duplicate descriptors may persist, but that is less disruptive than losing lifecycle/type information.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves some redundant entity descriptors, but preserves audit semantics that otherwise need local extensions or conventions.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 records using these entity fields become invalid in R6. Entity type and lifecycle can drive audit grouping and accountability, so silent loss is risky.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Removed entity fields fail R6 validation. R6 cannot reconstruct them unless preserved in detail, extensions, or related resources.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move entity.name to entity.what.display/identifier. Define explicit policy for entity.type and lifecycle, commonly profile-specific detail codings or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes optional entity descriptors that can be important for audit analysis. `entity.name` has a partial path through `entity.what.display`, but `entity.type` and especially `entity.lifecycle` have no exact replacement. Migration therefore risks either invalid R6 instances or local conventions that are not interoperable.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition includes AuditEvent.entity.type 0..1 Coding, entity.lifecycle 0..1 Coding, and entity.name 0..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition keeps entity.what, entity.role, securityLabel, description, query, detail, and entity.agent, but does not define entity.type, entity.lifecycle, or entity.name.
R6 entity.what comment says to use what.display when only a string such as ParticipantObjectName is available.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use softens the expectation compared with normative content, but audit entity classification and lifecycle are mature accountability data, so deletion carries a real stability burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 entity.type, entity.lifecycle, and entity.name are rejected by R6; lifecycle/type information can be lost unless profiles, extensions, or detail conventions are defined.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A practical less-breaking base design could have retained these optional elements as deprecated while recommending `what`, `role`, `securityLabel`, or detail-based conventions. The cost is some redundant descriptors, but it preserves legacy audit semantics that otherwise need local extensions.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as high impact with an available less-breaking base design.

findings.title: AuditEvent.entity.detail.type changed from string to CodeableConcept and detail values were broadened

oldState.summary: R4 detail.type was mandatory string; detail.value[x] allowed string or base64Binary.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 detail.type was mandatory string; detail.value[x] allowed string or base64Binary.

newState.summary: R6 detail.type is mandatory CodeableConcept; detail.value[x] retains R4 types and adds Quantity, CodeableConcept, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, time, dateTime, and Period.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 detail.type is mandatory CodeableConcept; detail.value[x] retains R4 types and adds Quantity, CodeableConcept, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, time, dateTime, and Period.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 detail.type strings fail R6 validation. R6 Quantity/Period/boolean/etc. detail values fail R4 validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep mandatory string `detail.type` and add an optional coded detail-type element while retaining the added R6 value[x] types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The value[x] broadening is mostly additive for R4-to-R6, but changing mandatory `detail.type` from string to CodeableConcept makes every legacy detail repetition invalid. A coded detail tag is a reasonable R6 goal, yet an optional companion coding could have captured that goal while preserving old string tags. Because the alternative is duplicative but localized and practical, the break is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could retain `entity.detail.type` as the R4 string and add a companion CodeableConcept field for interoperable coded tags, while still adding the new value[x] choices. The material tradeoff is duplicate tag fields and the need to define whether the string, the code, or both are required when both are present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old detail tags but duplicates tag semantics and complicates validation when both string and coded tags are present.

findings.narrativeMd: Every R4 detail repetition with a string tag needs conversion. R6 typed detail values cannot be downgraded without losing type information unless extensions are used.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 detail.type strings fail R6 validation. R6 Quantity/Period/boolean/etc. detail values fail R4 validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert string tags to CodeableConcept text/display or coding. Define downgrade rules for every new value type used, preserving units and precision.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R6 value[x] expansion is mostly additive for forward migration, but changing mandatory `entity.detail.type` from string to CodeableConcept invalidates every R4 detail repetition that uses the R4 tag string. The R6 comment gives a migration convention by putting a simple tag into CodeableConcept.display, which confirms the old use case remains valid but now requires a transform.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.entity.detail.type]: 1..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.entity.detail.type]: 1..1 CodeableConcept; definition says simple string tag names should use CodeableConcept.display.

R6 StructureDefinition snapshot.element[id=AuditEvent.entity.detail.value[x]] adds Quantity, CodeableConcept, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, time, dateTime, and Period while retaining string and base64Binary.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes this a moderate stability concern: detail is optional and implementation-defined, but when present the mandatory tag field is central to interpreting the detail value.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 detail.type strings fail the R6 CodeableConcept shape; new R6 typed values cannot be represented in R4 without stringifying or extensions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the string `detail.type` and added an optional coded tag element while still broadening value[x]. That duplicates tag semantics, but the duplication is localized and less disruptive than changing a mandatory child used by every detail entry.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and partial less-breaking alternative are supported; I classify it as Revisit because the alternative is practical and localized.

findings.title: New optional R6 elements create R6-to-R4 representability gaps

oldState.summary: R4 has no same-path fields for severity, basedOn, patient, encounter, or entity.agent.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has no same-path fields for severity, basedOn, patient, encounter, or entity.agent.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional severity, basedOn, patient, encounter, and entity.agent contentReference.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional severity, basedOn, patient, encounter, and entity.agent contentReference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 cannot carry these elements directly. Dropping them loses severity, workflow, patient/encounter context, or entity attribution.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; these are optional R6 additions and do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is a pure R6-to-R4 representability concern. Adding optional R6 fields for severity, workflow, patient, encounter, and entity attribution does not make any R4-valid AuditEvent invalid in R6. The R6 goal is reasonable and the compatibility issue belongs to downgrade policy rather than a backwards-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed for optional R6 additions. Systems that must downgrade to R4 can define extensions or loss policies, but those are migration mitigations rather than evidence that the R6 base design was unnecessarily breaking.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions or backports are downgrade mitigations, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

findings.narrativeMd: Optional additions do not break old R4 instances, but populated R6 data has no same-path R4 representation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 cannot carry these elements directly. Dropping them loses severity, workflow, patient/encounter context, or entity attribution.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define downgrade extensions or conventions for each new field; test disagreement between explicit patient/encounter and inferred entity context.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The listed R6 fields are optional additions. They can matter for downgrade policy, especially patient, encounter, severity, and entity-specific agent attribution, but they do not make any R4-valid AuditEvent invalid in R6. This is migration awareness for bidirectional bridges, not a design break in the R4-to-R6 direction.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition adds AuditEvent.severity 0..1 code, basedOn 0..* Reference(Resource), patient 0..1 Reference(Patient), encounter 0..1 Reference(Encounter), and entity.agent 0..* contentReference.
R4 StructureDefinition has no same-path elements for those added R6 fields.
All listed R6 additions have minimum cardinality 0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not turn optional additions into R4-to-R6 breaks. The audit/security domain means downgrade loss should be documented, but it does not require revisiting the base R6 additions.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: populated R6 additions have no direct R4 slots, so a downgrade must drop, extension-preserve, or map them by local convention.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for optional additions that preserve all R4 instances. Avoiding the new fields would reduce R6 expressiveness, and R4 backports or extensions are downgrade mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree that downgrade gaps exist, but the existing medium impact overstates the R4-to-R6 compatibility concern for optional additions.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not mark agent, source, or entity as summary.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local AuditEvent element semantics and neighboring paths.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid. Runtime summary views may include broader and differently shaped content.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 AuditEvent expressiveness, consistency, or accountability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; summary flag changes affect summary/runtime behavior, not R4 instance validity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: No R4-valid AuditEvent becomes invalid because local elements were newly marked summary in R6. The change may affect `_summary` payloads, generated summary views, or clients, but it is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base wire-format issue. Marking the alternative as not applicable better matches the calibration rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no relevant backwards-compatible base-design alternative for instance preservation. R6 could have retained the old summary flags to avoid runtime surprises, but that would trade off the R6 summary-use goal and is not the same as preserving R4 instance validity.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping R4 summary behavior would be a runtime compatibility choice, not a less-breaking instance-design alternative.

findings.narrativeMd: Summary flags do not affect instance validity but can change `_summary=true` payloads, generated summary DTOs, caches, and summary clients.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid. Runtime summary views may include broader and differently shaped content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review server summary serialization and clients parsing summary AuditEvents; add tests for agent/source/entity and new summary children.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition was possible for many of these changes through aliases, choice types, or profiles, but would have left duplicate or less precise modeling in the base resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The summary metadata changes can alter `_summary` payloads, generated summary views, and cache shapes, but they do not invalidate R4 instances. This should be a server/client regression-test item rather than a standards redesign concern, especially because the changed summaries sit alongside other intentional R6 structural changes.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: AuditEvent.agent, source, and entity are not marked isSummary.

R6 StructureDefinition: AuditEvent.agent, source, and entity are marked isSummary, and several R6 children such as severity, authorization, patient, outcome.code, and outcome.detail are summary elements.
No local AuditEvent isModifier change was identified for this finding.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use warrants checking runtime summary behavior, but summary flags are metadata/tooling behavior rather than an instance-validity break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: `_summary` serialization, generated DTOs, or summary-index expectations may change; base instance validation is unaffected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the old summary flags to reduce runtime surprises, but that is not a less-breaking instance-preservation design. Once R6 wants richer AuditEvent summaries, local client testing is the right mitigation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly says there is no hard instance break, but I view the medium impact as too high for a metadata/tooling-only concern.
